policy.acceptanceText: If you do not agree to this agreement, the submission policy, or maintainer review requirements, do not submit an app. If an accepted app later violates this agreement, maintainers may request changes, flag risk, delist, block, or retain audit records. The agreement may evolve with the project; material changes should be recorded publicly in the repository.
policy.agreementLead: This agreement applies to browsing, downloading, submitting, maintaining, or reviewing CardputerZero AppStore Hub apps, metadata, screenshots, binaries, and related discussions. Submitting an app means you have read and agree to these rules.
policy.agreementTitle: AppStore Hub User and Developer Agreement
device: Apps touching system settings, storage, network, sensors, or external modules must declare risk.
Apps must launch from APPLaunch and provide a clear exit path.
High CPU, storage, battery, or hardware risk must be visible on the detail page.
policy.lead: AppStore Hub puts user, device, maintainer, and open-source community trust first. Before submitting an app, developers must read and accept this agreement, privacy requirements, device-safety requirements, and rejection rules.
privacy: Apps must declare whether they collect, store, upload, or share user data.
Network, account, filesystem, and device identifier access must explain purpose.
Data collection should follow data minimization.
reject: Malware, credential theft, unauthorized persistence, or unauthorized access.
Hidden high-risk device behavior or undisclosed user-data collection.
Illegal, infringing, fraudulent, hateful, harassing, or harmful use.

sections.title: 1. Scope
items: This agreement covers app metadata, source code, binaries, icons, screenshots, README files, pull requests, issues, and comments submitted to the registry.
The Hub is a public directory and registry. It does not mean maintainers have performed a complete security audit for every app.
Before installing, users should review permissions, privacy, risk flags, source openness, download URLs, and checksums.

sections.title: 2. Developer responsibility
items: Developers must submit with a traceable GitHub identity and have the right to distribute all submitted code, assets, and binaries.
Developers must provide accurate, complete descriptions that do not mislead users or maintainers.
If download URLs, releases, source repositories, licenses, or app behavior changes, metadata should be updated promptly.

sections.title: 3. Metadata truthfulness
items: Network, filesystem, microphone, camera, sensors, GPS, external hardware, background service, and HDMI capabilities must be declared.
Source openness, license, commercial restrictions, version, checksum, dependencies, and device compatibility must be declared.
Paid limits, cloud services, account dependencies, high CPU, high storage, battery impact, or behavior that may damage user data must not be hidden.

sections.title: 4. Privacy and data
items: Apps that access, store, upload, or process user data must explain data type, purpose, retention, and third-party sharing.
Apps should follow data minimization and avoid collecting data unrelated to the feature.
If app behavior changes in a later version, the privacy declaration must be updated before or during release.

sections.title: 5. Device safety and UX
items: Apps must not intentionally damage the device, system files, user data, or external hardware.
GUI apps should fit the CardputerZero 320 x 170 screen and launch and exit correctly from APPLaunch.
Experimental, unfinished, special-setup, or device-risk apps must be clearly marked.

sections.title: 6. Prohibited content
items: Malware, spyware, credential theft, unauthorized persistence, unauthorized access, or review-bypass behavior is prohibited.
Illegal, infringing, fraudulent, phishing, impersonation, hateful, harassing, stalking, surveillance, weaponized, or harmful use is prohibited.
Hidden high-risk behavior, hidden commercial restrictions, unauthorized assets, or misleading install prompts are prohibited.

sections.title: 7. Review, listing, and delisting
items: Passing CI does not mean automatic listing; maintainers may request changes, additional declarations, demos, reproducible builds, or test logs.
Maintainers may mark apps as pending, ci-passed, approved, needs-changes, rejected, deprecated, or blocked.
Apps with clear user, device, legal, privacy, or community risk may be rejected, hidden, delisted, or blocked.

sections.title: 8. Appeals and records
items: Developers may appeal rejection, delisting, or blocked decisions through an issue or pull request.
Appeals should include app UUID, title, requested decision change, remediation notes, and evidence.
Maintainers should record final decisions where practical and may retain audit records without continuing to show install entries.

submit.agreementLead: Before publishing an app, read and accept the developer submission policy, privacy requirements, device-safety requirements, and rejection rules. Running czdev publish and opening a package pull request confirms that your metadata is truthful, permissions are complete, and you will cooperate with maintainer review.
submit.agreementTitle: Read the agreement and admission rules first
ci: Prepublish checks validate app-builder.json, the .deb control fields, APPLaunch .desktop, icons, screenshots, package name, and MD5.
Packages CI validates package metadata, Git LFS assets, APT index output, and registry generation inputs.
Passing CI does not mean automatic listing; maintainers still review policy, risk, and user experience.

submit.flowLead: Publish your source or release in your own GitHub repository first, then use czdev publish to submit the .deb, meta.json, icon, and screenshots to CardputerZero/packages.
submit.formatLead: Source app metadata lives in app-builder.json. The package pull request carries pool/main/<package>/meta.json with image paths relative to that package directory.
submit.lead: Developers publish installable .deb packages through czdev. After maintainer approval in CardputerZero/packages, the APT index is rebuilt and this Hub syncs generated registry JSON for the website and device AppStore.
metadata: app-builder.json needs a store section with summary, categories, icon, screenshots, and recommended zh-CN/en/ja locales.
The .deb must be arm64 and include APPLaunch .desktop, executable, and square PNG icon under /usr/share/APPLaunch.
Package metadata needs package name, MD5, published_at, updated_at, permissions, privacy behavior, external hardware, services, HDMI, commercial restrictions, and known risks.
review: In the package pull request description, explain the app purpose, test method, download source, and whether it has been validated on CardputerZero.
Closed-source, binary-only, network, microphone, filesystem, external hardware, and background-service apps receive stricter review.
Maintainers may request changes, extra declarations, experimental labeling, rejection, delisting, or blocking; appeals are recorded in issues or pull requests.

steps.title: Prepare your app repository
steps.body: Commit code to GitHub and provide README, license, build instructions, app-builder.json store metadata, icon, and screenshots.

steps.title: Build the package
steps.body: Build an arm64 .deb that installs APPLaunch files under /usr/share/APPLaunch and contains a square PNG icon.

steps.title: Run prepublish check
steps.body: Run the strict prepublish check against app-builder.json, source assets, .deb control fields, .desktop, icon, package name, and MD5.

steps.title: Publish with czdev
steps.body: Run czdev login once, optionally check czdev bump, then run czdev publish --deb <file.deb>.

steps.title: Review the package PR
steps.body: czdev opens a pull request against CardputerZero/packages. Describe device tests, privacy, permissions, and risks.

steps.title: Wait for release sync
steps.body: After maintainer approval and merge, the packages repo rebuilds the APT index and this Hub syncs generated registry JSON.

submit.structureLead: The submitted package directory stores meta.json, the .deb, icon, and four screenshots. The Hub registry is generated from package metadata.

tutorial.title: Development And Submission Tutorial
tutorial.lead: A practical path from local app development, Debian packaging, and device validation to prepublish checks, czdev publishing, and maintainer review.
tutorial.agreementTitle: Read The Agreement And Admission Rules First
tutorial.agreementLead: Running czdev publish and opening a package pull request confirms that metadata is truthful, permissions are complete, downloads are verifiable, and you will cooperate with maintainer review. Full rules now live in Documents.
tutorial.skillTitle: Develop With Skill And AI Coding
tutorial.skillLead: Use cardputer-zero-application for app quality and cardputer-app-publish for the czdev publish checklist, so AI confirms APPLaunch contracts, assets, package metadata, and device validation before release.
tutorial.flowLead: Click any step to see acceptance checks and linked documentation. The flow combines cardputer-zero-application APPLaunch validation with cardputer-app-publish czdev release checks.

devFlow.title: Build the app
devFlow.body: Keep source, README, license, build steps, and release history in your own GitHub repository.
checks: Choose the implementation language, app type, and launch mode first.
Decide whether the target is a 320 x 170 GUI, CLI utility, or background service.
Document dependencies, input model, exit behavior, known limits, and store metadata in README or app-builder.json.

devFlow.title: Package .deb
devFlow.body: Use APPLaunch-compatible paths and produce a Debian package installable on Raspberry Pi OS.
checks: Install files under the /usr/share/APPLaunch contract.
.desktop includes at least Name and Exec; Terminal is false by default.
Package must be arm64 and include package name, MD5, APPLaunch .desktop, and icon.

devFlow.title: Validate on device
devFlow.body: Check icon, launch, exit, permissions, peripherals, and framebuffer behavior on CardputerZero.
checks: Confirm the app launches from APPLaunch and returns cleanly.
Respect LV_LINUX_FBDEV_DEVICE instead of hard-coding /dev/fb0.
Test keyboard input, short Esc, long Home, or force-exit behavior.

devFlow.title: Prepare publish metadata
devFlow.body: Fill app-builder.json store metadata, locales, icon, four 320 x 170 screenshots, timestamps, permissions, privacy, and risk statements.
checks: Declare network, filesystem, microphone, hardware, and service behavior.
Describe source openness, license, and commercial-use restrictions.
Use ISO 8601 timestamps with seconds and explicit timezone.

devFlow.title: Publish with czdev
devFlow.body: Run the strict prepublish check, then use czdev login / bump / publish to create the package pull request.
checks: Prepublish check passes with no ERROR.
Package PR body includes purpose, test device, and validation result.
Mark experimental or device-risk behavior up front.

reviewFlow.title: Automated checks
reviewFlow.body: GitHub Actions validates package metadata, assets, APT Packages output, checksums, and registry generation.
checks: meta.json parses and image paths are package-relative.
Package name, MD5, SHA256, and APT index entries can be verified.
registry.json is generated, with registry-index.json kept as a legacy-compatible alias.

reviewFlow.title: Risk review
reviewFlow.body: Maintainers review source availability, sensitive permissions, services, hardware, privacy, and device safety.
checks: Sensitive capabilities match the app purpose.
Closed-source or binary-only apps include stronger disclosure.
Device, privacy, and legal risk take priority over app count.

reviewFlow.title: Change requests
reviewFlow.body: If declarations are incomplete or risks are unclear, maintainers request metadata, package, or test updates.
checks: Update metadata, package, or docs in the same PR.
Explain how each review point was handled.
Add screenshots, logs, or reproduction steps when needed.

reviewFlow.title: Merge and publish
reviewFlow.body: Approved package PRs rebuild the APT index; Hub sync then regenerates registry JSON and publishes through GitHub Pages.
checks: GitHub Pages can serve the synced registry.
Device AppStore sees the approved app after refresh.
Detail page, share code, and comments entry work.

reviewFlow.title: Maintain updates
reviewFlow.body: Publish a new package or metadata update when versions, screenshots, permissions, or behavior changes.
checks: Behavior changes update permissions and privacy first.
Broken downloads or wrong checksums are fixed quickly.
Unavailable or risky apps may be flagged, delisted, or blocked.
